description: Designing software that people can actually use: research, prototyping, interaction design, accessibility and evaluation, carried through a full design cycle with real users on real phones. Taught to the depth of a leading human-computer interaction design course.
modelledOn: Norman, The Design of Everyday Things
Rogers, Sharp and Preece, Interaction Design: Beyond Human-Computer Interaction
outcomes: Apply usability principles and Nielsen's heuristics to critique and improve an interface.
Plan and run user research with interviews, observation and surveys and synthesise personas and journey maps.
Produce sketches, wireframes and interactive prototypes at increasing fidelity.
Choose and apply interaction design patterns for navigation, input, feedback and error handling.
Design for accessibility and verify against WCAG with assistive technology.
Run usability tests and controlled studies, analyse the data, and design for low-bandwidth mobile users.

units.title: Foundations and usability principles
topics: Human-centred design and the design cycle; what usability means (ISO 9241)
Human capabilities: perception, memory, attention, Fitts's law, Hick's law, Gestalt principles
Norman's principles: affordances, signifiers, mapping, feedback, conceptual models
Nielsen's ten heuristics; heuristic evaluation of a Ghanaian banking app
Ethics in design: dark patterns, consent, inclusion

units.title: User research and personas
topics: Needfinding: interviews, contextual inquiry, observation, diary studies, surveys
Recruiting participants and research ethics; working across languages and literacy levels
Affinity diagrams and synthesis; personas, scenarios, journey maps, point-of-view statements
Task analysis and hierarchical task analysis
Field exercise: researching market traders, students or clinic staff

units.title: Ideation, prototyping and wireframes
topics: Brainstorming, sketching, storyboards, crazy eights
Low-fidelity paper prototypes and Wizard-of-Oz testing
Wireframes and information architecture; card sorting; navigation structures
Medium and high-fidelity prototypes in Figma or Penpot; design systems and components
Choosing fidelity for the question you need answered

units.title: Interaction design patterns and visual design
topics: Patterns for navigation, search, forms, lists, onboarding, notifications, empty states and errors
Direct manipulation, modes, undo, progressive disclosure, defaults
Visual design: layout and grids, typography, colour, hierarchy, icons; platform guidelines (Material, iOS)
Microinteractions, animation and feedback; responsiveness and perceived performance
Designing for voice, USSD and feature phones; multilingual interfaces

units.title: Accessibility
topics: Disability, situational impairment and universal design
WCAG principles (perceivable, operable, understandable, robust) and success criteria
Screen readers, keyboard navigation, captions, contrast, text size, motion
Testing with assistive technology and automated checkers; accessible forms and charts

units.title: Implementing interfaces
topics: Model-view-controller and component architectures; state and events
Building the prototype for real: web (HTML/CSS/JS or React) or mobile; responsive layout
Input handling, validation and feedback; offline states
Instrumenting an interface with analytics

units.title: Usability evaluation
topics: Formative versus summative evaluation; think-aloud usability testing; task design and metrics
Heuristic evaluation and cognitive walkthrough
Controlled experiments and A/B tests: hypotheses, variables, within and between subjects, basic statistics
Questionnaires: SUS, NASA-TLX; analysing qualitative data
Reporting findings and iterating on the design

units.title: Designing for low-bandwidth and mobile users
topics: Constraints: small screens, touch, intermittent 2G/3G, data cost, shared devices, low-end phones
Performance budgets, offline-first, progressive web apps, lightweight assets
Lessons from M-Pesa, WhatsApp, Jumia and USSD services
Final project: a complete design cycle from research to tested prototype

schedule.title: Human-centred design, human factors and Norman's principles
schedule.exercise: Redesign exercise: pick an everyday object or kiosk and annotate its affordances, signifiers, mapping and feedback, then sketch one improvement for each failing principle.

tasks.title: Judge six everyday interface photos in a scenario by naming the affordance, signifier and feedback that is missing in each
Work through a branching case on a ticket-machine redesign, applying Fitts's law and Hick's law to choose button size and menu length
Draw the human-centred design cycle for a bus-ticket app as a diagram, placing research, prototype and test activities with their inputs and outputs

schedule.title: Heuristic evaluation and design ethics
schedule.exercise: Evaluate three screens of a Ghanaian banking app against Nielsen's ten heuristics, rate each problem's severity, and write the top five fixes.

tasks.title: Evaluate a banking app transfer screen against Nielsen's ten heuristics and log each violation with its heuristic number and severity
Run a heuristic evaluation of a mobile money menu in a case scenario, merge the findings of three evaluators, and rank problems by severity
Review a sign-up flow in a branching case for dark patterns and consent problems, and decide which changes to demand, scoring against the ethics rubric

schedule.title: Needfinding and synthesis
schedule.exercise: Plan three user interviews on how traders manage stock, write the guide and consent text, then transform sample notes into an affinity diagram and one persona.

tasks.title: Choose the right method (interview, observation, diary or survey) for six research questions in a scenario and justify each choice
Prepare a consent script and recruit participants for a study at a rural clinic in a branching case, handling language and literacy needs
Synthesise twenty interview notes into an affinity diagram, one persona, one journey map and three point-of-view statements

schedule.title: Task analysis and a field study
schedule.exercise: Do a short field exercise: observe and write the hierarchical task analysis of a market trader selling and recording a sale, and list the pain points found.

tasks.title: Draw a hierarchical task analysis of withdrawing cash at an ATM with three levels of subtasks and a plan for each level
Build a hierarchical task analysis of a clinic registration process from supplied observations and mark the steps where errors are likely
Conduct a simulated field study of clinic staff in a branching case, choosing questions and observations to uncover three unstated needs

schedule.title: Ideation and low-fidelity prototyping
schedule.exercise: Run a crazy-eights session for a bus-arrival app, pick one idea, and produce a six-frame storyboard and three paper-prototype screens.

tasks.title: Sketch a six-frame storyboard of a farmer checking market prices on a phone, with each frame stating user, context and result
Draw the wireframes and information architecture of a school-fees payment app and label the navigation structure
Run a Wizard-of-Oz test of a paper prototype in a scenario, choosing tasks, handling unexpected user actions, and recording issues for scoring

schedule.title: Higher fidelity and choosing fidelity
schedule.exercise: Build a small component library with five reusable components and write a short rationale for what fidelity you used at each design stage.

tasks.title: Draw a design-system sheet with a colour palette, type scale, button and input components, and state the spacing rules
Choose the right prototype fidelity for five research questions in a case scenario, justifying the cost and the learning of each choice
Design a three-screen clickable flow for a mobile wallet using a shared component set, and annotate each interaction with its state change

schedule.title: Interaction patterns and visual design
schedule.exercise: Audit an app for navigation, form and error-message patterns, then redesign one form to apply progressive disclosure, sensible defaults and undo.

tasks.title: Wireframe an empty state, an error state and a loading state for a transport app's search screen
Redesign a long registration form using progressive disclosure and defaults, and show the reduced number of fields on the first screen
Create a visual hierarchy for a market-price screen using a grid, type scale and colour contrast, and justify each choice against platform guidelines

schedule.title: Feedback, microinteractions and low-resource interfaces
schedule.exercise: Design a USSD menu for checking a school-fees balance within a 160-character-per-screen limit and four steps, then write its test script.

tasks.title: Specify the feedback for a button press, a pending request and a failure on a payment screen in a short state diagram
Design a USSD menu tree for checking a balance and sending money in at most four steps, with every screen under 160 characters
Redesign a service for feature-phone users in a branching case with Twi and English menus, choosing between USSD, voice and SMS with evidence

schedule.title: Accessibility and universal design
schedule.exercise: Check one web page against four WCAG success criteria, record the failures, and rewrite the markup or design to fix each.

tasks.title: Classify twelve interface problems in a scenario under the four WCAG principles and mark each as a pass or a fail
Review a form in a case scenario for keyboard navigation, contrast and screen-reader labels, and decide the fix for each problem
Test a chart-heavy dashboard with simulated assistive technology in a branching case, and choose the fixes that bring it to AA conformance

schedule.title: Building the interface and instrumenting it
schedule.exercise: Specify an MVC structure for a small attendance app: list models, views, controllers, events, validation rules and the analytics events you would log.

tasks.title: Draw a model-view-controller diagram for a to-do app that lists the events passing between the three parts
Design the input validation and feedback states for a registration form including an offline state, and show them as a state diagram
Instrument a small web page so it logs clicks, errors and task times, then analyse the log to find the step where users drop out

schedule.title: Evaluation methods and experiments
schedule.exercise: Plan a five-person think-aloud test of a campus portal: write tasks, success criteria, metrics and a note-taking sheet, then run through a pilot.

tasks.title: Plan a think-aloud usability test in a scenario by writing three tasks, success measures and the questions to ask after each
Perform a cognitive walkthrough of an app's registration task in a case scenario, answering the four questions at each step
Analyse an A/B test of two checkout buttons, compute the conversion difference and p-value, and decide whether to ship the change

schedule.title: Questionnaires and reporting findings
schedule.exercise: Compute the SUS score from ten participants' responses, summarise the qualitative comments into themes, and write a one-page findings report with three prioritised changes.

tasks.title: Score ten System Usability Scale questionnaires, convert them to the 0 to 100 scale, and report the mean and range
Analyse think-aloud comments from six participants in a scenario into themes and rank each by frequency and severity
Prepare a findings report for a product team in a branching case, choosing which problems to fix first under a limited budget and justifying the order

schedule.title: Designing for low-resource contexts and the final project
schedule.exercise: Final project deliverable: a research summary, a tested prototype and a report on three iterations, for a service used on low-end phones with expensive data.

tasks.title: List the constraints of a rural user's phone, network and data budget in a scenario and match each constraint to a design response
Draw an offline-first architecture for a clinic-visit app, showing local storage, sync and the behaviour when the network drops
Complete a full design-cycle case from research to tested prototype, making every decision on method, fidelity and iteration for rubric scoring
